question: How much of llama.cpp's batch-1 decode on the RTX 5080 comes from PDL launches (M0.1 design §4.5, first task of step 3)?
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, driver <version>, power limit 360 W
llama_cpp: ggml-org/llama.cpp 51ce9c11a6f2dfa895696c0048c4333e8953b728, the spike S2 build (CUDA 13.0, CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120 -> 120a)
command: llama-bench -m Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf -p 0 -n 128 -ngl 99 -fa on -r 10 -o json, with and without GGML_CUDA_PDL=0; three interleaved rounds (default, off, default, off, ...)
result: PDL is worth +1.8 % tg128 (159.0 vs 156.2 t/s; 0.11 ms of a 6.29 ms token). Not launching our non-ggml kernels with PDL therefore costs at most about 2 % against this bar.
note: The S2 bar (tg128 >= 0.8 x 159.0 = 127 t/s) is measured with PDL on.
